ai.description: This small frog reaches 22–26 mm. It is brownish-grey with a distinct dark interorbital bar, white spots on the flanks, and a pale venter. It features a pointed snout and granular skin.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Raorchestes drutaahu* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, bright yellow or orange patch on its groin and the hidden surfaces of its thighs.
ai.habitat: *Raorchestes drutaahu* inhabits high-altitude evergreen forests and shola grasslands in the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Fast-calling Shrub Frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining active at night to forage for small invertebrates among the foliage of its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Raorchestes drutaahu* exhibits direct development, bypassing the tadpole stage. It breeds during the monsoon, laying small clutches of eggs in arboreal nests.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Raorchestes drutaahu* is endemic to the high-altitude evergreen forests of the Western Ghats in Karnataka, India, typically found at elevations above 1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Fast-calling Shrub Frog emits a high-pitched, rapid series of metallic "tink" notes, typically heard from vegetation in high-altitude montane forests.
